value_chain.value_chain_position: Application layer specializing in AI-powered audio generation and voice synthesis. ElevenLabs develops its own proprietary audio AI models (Eleven v3, Flash v2.5, Music model) in-house, giving it partial model-creator capabilities, but its primary market position is as an application and API provider. Depends on cloud infrastructure (AWS, with EU data residency options) and GPU compute (NVIDIA investor). Serves both individual creators (bottom-up adoption) and enterprises (Fortune 500 customers) through a self-serve platform and API. Positioned as the dominant voice layer that other AI applications integrate: partnerships with Perplexity (AI search), Synthesia and HeyGen (AI video), and direct enterprise deployments for conversational AI agents, dubbing, and customer support automation.

key_products: Text-to-Speech API and Platform (Eleven v3, Flash v2.5): industry-leading voice synthesis with nuanced intonation, emotional awareness, and multilingual support across 32 languages. Eleven v3 delivers the highest quality naturalistic speech; Flash v2.5 optimized for real-time applications with ~75ms latency. Used by 41% of Fortune 500 companies. API-first design enables integration into any application. Voice Marketplace allows creators to monetize AI voice clones, creating network effects.

ElevenLabs Agents (Conversational AI): complete platform for launching voice-based conversational agents that talk, type, and take action across phone, web, and apps. Includes phone integration, knowledge bases, and action capabilities. Targets enterprise use cases: customer support (Revolut), inbound sales, citizen engagement (Ukrainian Government), and internal training. Key growth driver for enterprise ARR.

Dubbing Studio and Eleven Music: Dubbing Studio enables full movie/video dubbing with AI-generated transcripts, translations, and timecodes across 29 languages. Eleven Music (launched Aug 2025) generates studio-grade music from natural language prompts, cleared for commercial use in film, TV, podcasts, ads, and gaming. Additional products include Reader App (iOS/Android for listening to articles/PDFs/ePubs) and Speech-to-Text transcription.

business.revenue_or_valuation: Valued at $11B as of February 2026 (Series D). ARR reached $330M+ by end of 2025, up from approximately $120M at end of 2024 (175% YoY growth). Company went from $200M to $300M ARR in just 5 months during 2025. Eyeing potential IPO.
business.annual_recurring_revenue_arr: $330M+ ARR as of end of 2025 (Sacra estimate). Growth trajectory: ~$120M ARR end of 2024 -> $200M ARR by mid-2025 -> $330M+ ARR by end of 2025. Represents 175% year-over-year growth. Enterprise adoption by Deutsche Telekom, Square, Revolut, Ukrainian Government, and 41% of Fortune 500 driving growth.
business.funding_total_and_last_round: Total raised: $781M across 5 rounds. Rounds: $2M Pre-Seed (Jan 2023), $19M Series A at ~$100M valuation (Jun 2023), $80M Series B at $1.1B valuation (Jan 2024, Andreessen Horowitz/others), $180M Series C at $3.3B valuation (Jan 2025), $500M Series D at $11B valuation (Feb 2026, Sequoia Capital lead, with a16z, Iconiq, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Bond). Strategic investors include Deutsche Telekom, LG Technology Ventures, HubSpot Ventures.
business.business_model: Hybrid subscription + usage-based pricing. Self-serve tiers: Free (20K credits/month), Creator ($22/mo, 100K credits), Pro ($99/mo, 500K credits), Scale ($330/mo, 500K credits), Business ($1,320/mo, 11M credits). Each text character consumes credits; newer models offer discounted credit rates. API included in all plans at no extra cost beyond credit consumption. Enterprise tier with custom pricing, dedicated support, data residency options, and SLA guarantees. Revenue mix shifting toward enterprise as conversational AI agents and dubbing drive larger contracts.
business.burn_rate_and_runway: [uncertain] Not publicly disclosed. Reports suggest ElevenLabs achieved operating profitability by late 2024, which would be exceptional for its growth stage. With $781M raised, $330M+ ARR, and potential profitability, runway is effectively unlimited. Headcount of ~690 employees as of Jan 2026 suggests significant but manageable operating costs relative to revenue.

openness.open_vs_closed_spectrum: Closed / Hybrid. Core voice synthesis models (Eleven v3, Flash v2.5, Music) are fully proprietary with no open weights or source code. API access is open to all (including free tier), making the technology highly accessible without being open-source. ElevenLabs hosts some open-source models on its platform. The company launched an Engineers OSS Fund to support open-source projects it depends on (compilers, frameworks, tooling), but its own models remain closed. Terms explicitly prohibit reverse engineering or extracting model weights.

startup_relevance.relevance_for_startups: ElevenLabs is highly relevant for entrepreneurship students as both a building block for AI products and a case study in European AI success: (1) API-first platform for builders: unlike Harvey's enterprise-only model, ElevenLabs offers a free tier and developer-friendly API that any startup can integrate immediately, making it the default voice layer for AI applications -- if you are building anything with voice (chatbots, audiobooks, accessibility tools, content localization), ElevenLabs is likely the first integration you evaluate; (2) European AI success story: founded by two Polish engineers, headquartered in London, with a $11B valuation -- ElevenLabs proves that world-class AI companies can be built from Europe, directly relevant for French/EU entrepreneurship context; (3) Product-led growth masterclass: ElevenLabs grew from $0 to $330M ARR in 3 years through bottom-up developer adoption (free tier, viral voice cloning demos) that converted into enterprise contracts -- a textbook PLG case study; (4) Vertical integration strategy: unlike most AI application companies that are pure model consumers, ElevenLabs develops its own proprietary models in-house with a 7-person elite research team, creating true technical differentiation that cannot be replicated by wrapping OpenAI APIs; (5) Voice marketplace and network effects: the Voice Library where creators monetize AI voice clones creates two-sided network effects (more voices attract more users, more users attract more voice creators), providing a data and distribution moat; (6) Multimodal expansion: the move from TTS into music generation, dubbing, conversational agents, and transcription shows how a startup can expand from a single AI capability into a full-stack audio platform; (7) Potential profitability at scale: reported operating profitability by late 2024 while growing 175% YoY challenges the assumption that AI companies must burn cash indefinitely.
startup_relevance.accessibility: Very high accessibility. Free tier with 20,000 credits/month requires only email signup. API access included in all plans, even free. Creator plan at $22/month suitable for MVP-stage startups. Pro at $99/month for production use. Comprehensive documentation, SDKs for Python and JavaScript, and community support. Enterprise tier for larger deployments with custom pricing and EU data residency. No minimum commitment on self-serve plans. One of the most startup-accessible AI platforms available.
startup_relevance.primary_model_dependency: None (primary). ElevenLabs develops its own proprietary audio AI models in-house (Eleven v3, Flash v2.5, Music model). Does not depend on OpenAI, Anthropic, or other foundation model providers for its core voice synthesis capabilities. May use third-party models for ancillary features but core technology is fully proprietary.

ecosystem.competitive_moat: Proprietary model quality: in-house research team produces voice synthesis quality that consistently leads benchmarks, creating true technical differentiation vs. competitors using third-party models. Developer ecosystem and API ubiquity: API-first design with free tier has made ElevenLabs the default voice integration for AI applications, similar to how Stripe became default for payments. Voice Marketplace network effects: two-sided marketplace where creators monetize voice clones attracts both supply (voice actors) and demand (developers/content creators), creating a flywheel competitors cannot easily replicate. Enterprise trust and adoption: 41% of Fortune 500 penetration creates reference-ability and switching costs. Multilingual coverage: 32-language support with high quality across all languages creates a global moat vs. English-focused competitors. Full audio stack: expansion from TTS into music, dubbing, transcription, and conversational agents means customers consolidate audio needs on one platform, increasing switching costs.

regulatory.regulatory_exposure: GPAI provider (likely). As a developer of proprietary AI models that generate synthetic audio content, ElevenLabs likely falls under GPAI provider obligations in the EU AI Act. Voice cloning technology raises specific concerns around deepfakes and synthetic media, addressed by EU AI Act transparency requirements (Article 50: AI-generated content must be labeled). ElevenLabs has proactively invested in safety measures (voice verification, no-go voice detection, content moderation) and offers EU data residency. The company has EU-specific Terms of Use acknowledging AI Act applicability. High-risk classification could apply when voice agents are used for customer-facing decisions in regulated sectors.
